Compute stereonet coordinates for a line (radians)

Source: R/dir-utils.R
StCoordLine.Rd

Converts the trend and plunge of a line to its \((x, y)\) position on an equal-area or equal-angle stereonet of unit radius.

Usage

StCoordLine(trd, plg, wulff = F)

Arguments

trd

Numeric. Trend of the line in radians.

plg

Numeric. Plunge of the line in radians. Lines plunging into the upper hemisphere (negative plunge) are automatically reflected.

wulff

Logical. If TRUE uses an equal-angle (Wulff) projection; if FALSE (default) uses an equal-area (Schmidt) projection.

Value

A one-row matrix with columns xp and yp giving the stereonet coordinates.

References

Allmendinger, R. W., Cardozo, N., & Fisher, D. M. (2012). Structural geology algorithms: Vectors and tensors. Cambridge university press.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Triple colon required because it's not exported
GMisc:::StCoordLine(trd = pi / 4, plg = pi / 6)
GMisc:::StCoordLine(trd = pi / 3, plg = pi / 4, wulff = TRUE)
} # }
